```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Feasibility within 90 days favors A. It can ship as a deliberately thin product (upload, OTP/SSO, directory). B's stated differentiator, filing in the country of residence, requires liability-bearing tax logic across multiple jurisdictions. The brief itself says the most advanced competitor calls this the unsolved 'hard part.'",
    "B has regulatory gates before it can take money for e-filed returns: IRS EFIN application with a suitability check, annual IRS software acceptance testing, and EU data-protection counsel review. The brief lists the e-file authorization timeline as an open question, so it may not fit inside 90 days. A's brief lists no comparable licensing barrier.",
    "B is paid once per filing season. Depending on when the 90-day window falls, there may be no buying moment at all. A is a monthly subscription that can be bought any time.",
    "A's acquisition channels are low-cost and sourced: Product Hunt at about $3–5 blended CPA, free marketplace listings, and Show HN at $0. B's only channel is Meta lead-gen at a $27.66 cross-industry average CPL. The brief says the finance vertical likely runs higher than that.",
    "A has sourced, public paid tiers for a near-identical thin product: display.dev at €15–49/mo and Volly at $75/mo per workspace. These show a small-ticket self-serve purchase exists. If B drops the local-filing half, it becomes a crowded US-only market priced at $67–$219 that still needs IRS authorization.",
    "B's demand evidence is stronger, with three independent Reddit quotes including $800–$2,500 accountant quotes. A's is weak: one vendor-curated testimonial and one Reddit post about difficulty sharing tools, not about paying. A wins on reachability of a first paying customer, not on demand strength."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's case for leans on the claim that Atamatax, built solo, 'can charge $199-$799 and attract customers,' and treats this as validation of a one-person build. The cited source supports only the published prices. The brief gives no evidence of customer count, revenue, or conversion, so the 'attract customers' part is effectively unsourced and should count as missing.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. A's independent demand evidence is thin, and it faces at least five near-identical competitors with no identified wedge, plus a real sandboxing security liability. B has clearer pain and willingness to pay. The pick rests mainly on B's scope, regulatory gates, and seasonality making a paying customer within 90 days unlikely, not on A being proven."
}
```
